newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Fewer ship arrivals hits Rotterdam bunkers - repor.
newsitem.headline: Fewer ship arrivals hits Rotterdam bunkers - repor.

text.p: The number of ships calling at Rotterdam is steadily falling and, although the size of ships is growing, bunker fuel suppliers feel they may be losing out.
Last year, the number of ships arriving fell by six to seven percent, according to Dirk Zwager, a private agency which monitors shipping movements in Rotterdam.
This year, it says, the trend is continuing, despite a reasonably active January.
In January, some 2,573 ships arrived in Rotterdam, compared with 2,586 in January 1996, but in February, ship arrivals declined by seven percent, from 2,417 to 2,248.
"It seems partly to do with the economic situation, but certainly ships are gradually getting bigger," a company spokesman said.
Bunker suppliers in Rotterdam say fuel oil volumes have been notably poor this year and that the trend towards fewer larger ships may be partly to blame.
"Demand is certainly more erratic. Shipowners can wait much longer. It's very much more a buyers' market," one Rotterdam-based supplier said.

The Rotterdam bunker market had plentiful enquiries at the end of this week. The buying came partly from shipowners who had delayed purchases until a market dip and partly from those restocking ahead of Easter holidays.
However, many in the market complain the good days are getting fewer.
"(A daily volume of) 20,000 tonnes, like today, is not really all that special. Ten suppliers have to live off that," one Rotterdam dealer said.
"The last really good day was last year," said another.
